target.title: fix(media): accept repeated content-length when values match
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where media and plugin paths that rely on shared Content-Length parsing could reject otherwise valid responses when response headers expose repeated matching Content-Length values as a comma-joined header value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared media parser now parses each comma-separated Content-Length member with the existing digit and safe-integer checks, then accepts the header only when every parsed value agrees. Malformed, unsafe, empty, or conflicting values still fail before body reads, so callers keep their existing byte-cap decisions in one owner-local helper.

## User Impact

Users and plugin/channel developers are less likely to see valid media, auth, or download responses fail solely because an upstream server or proxy repeated an identical Content-Length header. Conflicting or malformed headers are still rejected.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: `parseMediaContentLength` accepts single values and matching repeated values while rejecting malformed, unsafe, empty, and disagreeing values.
- Current-head proof at `ab5a5fad20c85836fbea63fa41e39006d4dbf065`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/media-core/src/content-length.test.ts` passed in `E:\code\openclaw-lane-e`.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the focused test exercises the shared parser used by media and Plugin SDK Content-Length callers.
